title: Barbara Kruger

description.main: The catalogue of Barbara Kruger's 2014 solo exhibition at Modern Art Oxford, with a foreword by Paul Hobson and essays by Ciara Moloney and Timothy Williamson.
description.extended:
This softcover is the catalogue of Barbara Kruger's 2014 solo exhibition at Modern Art Oxford, printed in an edition of 1,500 copies.

The exhibition ran from 28 June to 31 August 2014. In the Upper Gallery Kruger covered the walls from top to bottom with a new text work in black, white and green, colours rarely seen in her work, posing questions such as "IS THERE LIFE WITHOUT PAIN?" The Middle Gallery paired paste-ups from the 1980s with the film Plenty LA (2008), and the Piper Gallery held a four-screen installation of Twelve (2004).

The 64-page book reproduces the text of the Upper Gallery wrap, examples of the 1980s paste-ups and stills from Twelve. Director Paul Hobson writes the foreword. The essays are by Ciara Moloney, the gallery's Curator of Exhibitions and Projects, who edited the volume, and by Timothy Williamson, Wykeham Professor of Logic at the University of Oxford.
description.artist_bio: Barbara Kruger (b. 1945, Newark) is an American artist who pairs found photographs with declarative text. She worked as a designer and picture editor at Conde Nast magazines, including Mademoiselle, before turning to photocollage in the late 1970s. She received the Golden Lion for lifetime achievement at the 51st Venice Biennale in 2005.
description.exhibition_context: Modern Art Oxford showed a new site-specific text wrap in the Upper Gallery, 1980s paste-ups with Plenty LA (2008) in the Middle Gallery, and the four-screen Twelve (2004) in the Piper Gallery.

notes: Published on the occasion of the exhibition at Modern Art Oxford, 28 June to 31 August 2014. Softcover, 64 pages (Library of Congress counts 63 numbered pages), 21 x 27 cm, edition of 1,500 per the ICA Bookstore listing. The ICA listing refers to the exhibition as Untitled (Titled); Modern Art Oxford's announcement titles it simply Barbara Kruger. The Google Books record for this ISBN carries a description of an unrelated earlier US catalogue. Ciara Moloney is listed as curator on the strength of the ICA listing and her later Paragon Studios biography, which says she organized the Kruger exhibition.
